title: When AI Should Not Decide: Evidence Sufficiency and Decision Stability in Automated Job Interviews
abstract: arXiv:2611.28426v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly used to assess employment candidates, yet consistent interview scoring does not establish whether automated recommendations are supported by sufficient evidence. This study introduces the Evidence Sufficiency and Decision Stability Assessment (ESDSA), which combines criterion-level evidence classification, deterministic quotation traceability and stability checks across linguistic variants assessed as substantively equivalent. We evaluated four approaches (scoring-only, evidence-aware, traceability-based and integrated ESDSA v2) using 540 synthetic interview responses from 60 evaluated scenario families across Software Engineering, Customer Support and Operations. In held-out testing (216 responses), integrated ESDSA achieved 85.19% actionable coverage and 3.80% disagreement among actionable recommendations against AI-assisted provisional references. translated_title: 何时AI不应做决策：自动化求职面试中的证据充分性与决策稳定性
translated_abstract: 人工智能越来越多地被用于评估求职候选人，然而一致的面试评分并不能确立自动化建议是否得到了充分证据的支持。本研究提出了证据充分性与决策稳定性评估（ESDSA）框架，该框架结合了标准层面的证据分类、确定性的引文可追溯性，以及在实质等同的语言变体上进行的稳定性检验。我们使用来自软件工程、客户支持和运营领域60个评估场景族的540份合成面试回答，评估了四种方法（仅评分、证据感知、基于可追溯性和集成式ESDSA v2）。在留出测试集（216份回答）中，集成式ESDSA实现了85.19%的可操作覆盖率，且相对于AI辅助的临时参考，可操作建议之间的分歧率仅为3.80%。证据感知评估实现了92.59%的覆盖率……
tldr: 本研究提出证据充分性与决策稳定性评估框架（ESDSA），通过证据分类、引文溯源和语言变体稳定性检验来判断AI自动化面试评估建议是否有足够证据支撑，在留出测试中实现了85.19%的可操作覆盖率且建议分歧率仅3.80%。
en_tdlr: This study introduces the Evidence Sufficiency and Decision Stability Assessment (ESDSA) framework, which combines evidence classification, quotation traceability, and stability checks across linguistic variants to determine whether AI recommendations in automated job interviews are sufficiently evidence-supported, achieving 85.19% actionable coverage with only 3.80% disagreement in held-out testing.
